Varda designs, builds and flies its W-Series vehicles in-house: the satellite bus, the reentry capsule, the heat shield and the pharmaceutical payload. We are moving from a few missions a year to a steady flight cadence, serving pharmaceutical, defense and research customers under commercial and government contracts, and standing up new production and laboratory space to do it. No one has run a factory whose output flies to orbit, processes a drug in microgravity and comes home through the atmosphere at hypersonic speed. The component portfolio spans each of these fluid subsystems and includes solenoid control valves, check valves, relief valves, burst disks, fluid filters, regulators, manually operated service valves, machined fluid manifolds, and instrumentation including pressure transducers and RTDs. A successful candidate will take on a significant share of the component ownership for these mission-critical hardware articles as responsible engineer, helping expand component capabilities, improve reliability, and increase flight cadence. Many current Varda components are purchased parts, and you will be a primary technical interface to our suppliers. Varda also intends to bring more component design in-house for current and future vehicles, and you will help lead that transition: shaping make-versus-buy decisions, executing detailed design, and standing up the capabilities to develop, qualify, produce, acceptance test, and fly Varda-owned parts. jobs.title: Senior GRC Engineer II
jobs.description_text: As a Sr Security Engineer II on the Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team, you will play a central role in strengthening and sustaining our cybersecurity posture, policy governance, and regulatory compliance programs. Operating within the Information Security GRC team, you will serve as a primary steward of Aledade’s security policies, policy governance, cyber risk management frameworks, and continuous audit readiness. In this role, you will act as the key liaison and point person for security risk intake, providing expert risk advisory, trade-off analysis, and actionable guidance to cross-functional stakeholders across Engineering, IT, Legal, Product, and Business Operations. You will directly maintain and manage Aledade’s InfoSec issue tracker and risk register, ensuring that security findings, control gaps, and risk mitigations are rigorously documented, assigned, and tracked to closure. Furthermore, you will work closely with your manager to produce and report monthly and quarterly KPIs and metrics for leadership, as well as facilitate key audit and assessment engagements—including SOC 2 Type 2 attestation, SOX ITGC testing, HIPAA/HITRUST reviews, NIST 800-53 assessments, and other internal assessments—ensuring seamless evidence collection, auditor coordination, and continuous compliance across Aledade's healthcare ecosystem.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager – Camera Firmware Platform
jobs.description_text: About the Team The Camera Firmware Platform team owns the foundation that every Verkada camera runs on. While our product firmware teams bring new camera categories to market, this team makes every camera in the fleet, both existing and future models, more reliable, faster, leaner, and more power-efficient. Edge Storage: We own the on-camera storage stack that turns every Verkada camera into a self-contained recording device. Our mandate is reliable, accessible, secure, and observable storage of customer video. Footage is preserved instantly across SD cards and raw NAND, even during network outages or sudden power loss, for millions of cameras and petabytes of video. This extends to the backend services that manage retention, cloud backup, and storage health across the fleet. Firmware Platform: Building on that foundation, we own the cross-cutting firmware systems underneath every camera feature: boot and shutdown, memory and power management, system state orchestration, IPC, observability, and firmware update. We build these once, for every camera model and SoC, so product teams can move fast without rebuilding the same infrastructure. About the Role As the Engineering Manager for Camera Firmware Platform, you will lead a highly technical team of storage and embedded systems engineers responsible for the reliability, performance, power, and stability of firmware running on a fleet of more than 1.8 million perpetually online devices. jobs.description_text: The Opportunity Every day, a security administrator somewhere decides who can open which door. A new nurse starts on Monday and needs the medication room but not the server closet. A contractor needs the loading dock for three weeks. Someone leaves the company at 5pm and their badge should stop working at 5:01. Multiply that by 200,000 employees across 400 sites, and you have one of the largest and least-solved logistical problems in enterprise software. Access control is Verkada's second largest business: hundreds of millions of dollars in sales, growing 40 to 60% year over year, with roughly 80 people building in this area. Access management is the pillar that decides whether all of that feels effortless or exhausting. We are hiring a Lead Product Manager to own it end to end: users, identities, groups, policies, requests, access levels, and visitor access, from the moment an admin expresses intent to the moment a door opens for the right person. We do this well today. We think it can be dramatically better, through interfaces that make scale feel simple, APIs and integrations that let the system run itself, and agents that let an admin state what they want instead of clicking through configuration. jobs.description_text: The Opportunity Every day, a security administrator somewhere decides who can open which door. Multiply that by 200,000 employees across 400 sites, and you have one of the largest and least-solved logistical problems in enterprise software. Access control is Verkada's second largest business: hundreds of millions of dollars in sales, growing 40 to 60% year over year, with roughly 80 people building in this area. Access management is the pillar that decides whether all of that feels effortless or exhausting. The US air and missile defense enterprise was assembled over four decades, one program at a time. Army air defense runs on one battle manager, short range air defense on another, the ballistic missile defense system on a third, and the fleet on a fourth. Each of them was engineered well for the threat it was scoped against. None of them was designed to be extended by anyone other than the prime that built it, which is why adding a sensor or an effector to an existing architecture is still a multi-year integration program rather than a software release. That is the opening we are working. A software-defined fire control layer, built on Lattice, with interfaces open enough that a new sensor, a new interceptor, or a new effects chain can be brought in at the pace software moves rather than the pace a hardware program moves. The technical case is strong and the early programs are real. What we need now is someone who can turn that into share inside programs of record.
